thread:
matt: Ran an apples-to-apples comparison for the kernel-selection change, server binary unchanged, but client harness shows ~15% higher p50. anyone seen similar artifacts?
liya: Did you warm the KV cache and prime sockets? small differences there can look like regressions.
ahmed: Also check the client connection model. Are you replaying sessions or issuing fresh connections per request? HTTP1 new TLS handshake per req will kill p50.
matt: Replay harness uses a python script that creates a new requests.Session() per virtual user, but each request does a new POST to /generate. I assumed keepalive was on by default.
sophia: In many languages "keepalive" at the HTTP layer is orthogonal to the transport pool size. Python requests will reuse sockets if you reuse the session object; spawning sessions per VU behaves like cold-connections.
liya: For an apples-to-apples test vs gRPC you must match multiplexing semantics. gRPC (http2) reuses a single connection, so it avoids TLS and Nagle overhead per request. Comparing that to HTTP/1.1 persistent but low pool-size is noisy.
matt: Good point. The weird part: when I switched to a Go-based loadgen with http.Transport and large MaxIdleConnsPerHost, p50 dropped back down. So it's definitely client-side.
ahmed: Check Nagle / TCP_NODELAY — Go's net library historically leaves Nagle enabled unless data framing forces flush. For small JSON payloads you can hit coalescing delays. On the client side set TCP_NODELAY on the socket or aggregate requests into larger packets.
sophia: Also TLS session resumption: first-time handshakes add ~15ms on our infra. If your replay harness reuses connections then the server tail looks better. Your runs need an explicit warmup period that mirrors production connection churn.
liya: Kernel selection effects can also interact with socket behavior. New kernel path might change tcp_early_retransmit/tcp_congestion algo defaults which affects small-packet egress timing. So you can see a change even though app-level code didn't change.
matt: We captured flamegraphs and perf profiles; user CPU identical, but syscalls/spend in sendmsg grew. That points to more expensive TLS write path or more syscalls due to new connection churn.
ahmed: On the client harness side, confirm thread/worker pinning. If the loadgen's workers are moved across cores you pay scheduling jitter which shows in p50. Pin load threads and the generator to stable CPUs.
sophia: For deterministic apples-to-apples docs I usually recommend:
```
- use same client library + version (go/python/java)
- match connection reuse model (http1 keepalive pool size or single http2 channel)
- warm KV and model caches with N warm requests (same prefix lengths)
- run a short priming phase that opens connections and warms TLS session caches
- pin loadgen threads and set identical batch sizes/batching heuristics
- capture perf + syscall traces on both client and server
```
liya: Also watch out for Nagle vs batching heuristics in the runtime: if your serving runtime switched kernel-level send coalesce behavior, small-token streaming can accumulate into fewer but larger writes or more fragmented writes depending on send() sizes. That shifts latency distributions.
matt: How do you recommend simulating realistic prefix cache hits? Our replay harness replays a mix but distribution might be off.
sophia: Capture production prefix length histogram and replay the same distribution. Also include prefix reuse (same session repeating) to exercise KV cache hit rates. Don't rely on uniformly random sequences.
ahmed: Quick sanity checks:
- curl test: `curl -v --http1.1 -H "Connection: keep-alive" -X POST https://host/generate` to confirm keepalive reuse
- go snippet: `tr := &http.Transport{MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 200, IdleConnTimeout: 90*time.Second}` to ensure pool isn't tiny
- tcp: use `setsockopt(IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_NODELAY, 1)` on the client for microbench experiments

matt: Thanks — I'll re-run with a pinned Go loadgen, explicit warmup, and matched connection reuse vs our gRPC baseline. Will report traces.
perf-bot: perf-regression-detector: flagged run 1715000000 as anomalous (p50 delta +14%). Manual triage recommended. :warning:
